title: Public Wi-Fi
about: Spot fake Wi-Fi, and keep money off public Wi-Fi.

cards.prompt: Three Wi-Fi networks show up at the Corner Café. **Tap each glowing thing.**

parts.job: The café's own Wi-Fi box. It sends the network CornerCafe.
Someone's laptop. Its owner named a network CornerCafe_Free.
The library next door. It sends the network Library_Guest.

cards.explanation: Three networks, three owners: the café, a stranger's laptop and the library.

cards.prompt: Sam joins CornerCafe_Free. It asks for Sam's email password. **Tap who gets it.**

image.alt: Left: Sam's phone shows a page: Free Wi-Fi! Sign in with your email password, a password box and a finger on Go. Right, dimmed with question marks: the café counter with its Wi-Fi box and a staff member, a laptop on table 4, and a button: Nobody.
image.revealAlt: A dotted line runs from Sam's phone to the laptop at table 4, where a bubble with the hidden password lands.

cards.explanation: The laptop's owner made this network and its page, so whatever Sam types goes to them.

cards.title: Public Wi-Fi and fake Wi-Fi
cards.body: On **public Wi-Fi**, anyone can name a network after the café. A copycat like CornerCafe_Free is **fake Wi-Fi**: its name can look just right.

image.alt: The Wi-Fi list, labelled. CornerCafe, from the café's Wi-Fi box, is public Wi-Fi. CornerCafe_Free, from someone's laptop, is fake Wi-Fi.

cards.prompt: Sam wants the café's real Wi-Fi this time. **Tap the best way** to find its name.

image.alt: Sam's Wi-Fi list: CornerCafe with two bars and CornerCafe_Free with four bars. Below, the café counter with its Wi-Fi box and a staff member in an apron.
image.revealAlt: The staff member says: It's CornerCafe. That row in the list is ticked.

options.text: Ask the staff which one is theirs
Join the one with the most bars
options.nudge: Could a laptop close to Sam have strong bars too?

options.text: Join the one with Free in its name

cards.explanation: Staff know their own network's name, so you're not guessing from names and bars.
cards.showAnswer: Ask the staff: anyone can pick a name, and a laptop nearby can have strong bars.

cards.prompt: Some jobs are too important for Wi-Fi you can't be sure of. **Drag** each into a bin.
cards.explanation: Everyday browsing is fine; for money and important accounts, mobile data skips any fake Wi-Fi.
cards.nudge: Which ones involve your money or your most important accounts?
cards.showAnswer: Videos and news are fine; your bank and important passwords go on mobile data.

cards.prompt: At the airport, you want to buy a game on your phone. **Tap how you'll go online.**

image.alt: An airport sign: Free Wi-Fi: Airport Wi-Fi. Your phone's list below it: Airport Wi-Fi, Airport_Free, and a separate switch, Mobile data. A game shop page waits with a Buy button.
image.revealAlt: Mobile data is switched on and the Wi-Fi networks are greyed out. The Buy button now says Bought.

options.nudge: A matching name is great for browsing: what kind of job is buying a game?
Who chose that name, and does it match the sign?

cards.explanation: Buying is money, so mobile data means you don't have to guess which Wi-Fi is real.
cards.showAnswer: Mobile data: buying is money, and on public Wi-Fi you can't always be sure which network is real.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
Anyone can name Wi-Fi after the café: **ask staff** for the real one, and use **mobile data** for money.

**Try this:** Next time you're out, ask staff for the Wi-Fi name before you join.

**Next:** The clues that someone else has got into your account.
